events.title: United States Declares War on Britain
events.description: President James Madison signed the declaration of war passed by Congress. It began the War of 1812 against the United Kingdom. The dispute centered on British trade restrictions, the impressment of American sailors, and tensions on the frontier.
events.significance: It was the first time the United States formally declared war. The conflict boosted American national identity and shaped relations with Britain and Canada.

events.title: Battle of Waterloo
events.description: Near a small Belgian village, the Duke of Wellington and Prussian Field Marshal Gebhard Leberecht von Blücher defeated Napoleon Bonaparte. Napoleon was forced to abdicate as French emperor for the second and final time.
events.significance: Waterloo ended more than two decades of nearly continuous European war. It closed the Napoleonic era and set the stage for a long period of relative peace among Europe's great powers.

events.title: Amelia Earhart Crosses the Atlantic by Air
events.description: Amelia Earhart became the first woman to fly across the Atlantic Ocean in an aircraft. She was a passenger on the flight, with Wilmer Stultz as pilot and Lou Gordon as mechanic.
events.significance: The flight made Earhart an international celebrity. It launched the career that would make her one of the most celebrated figures in aviation history.

events.title: De Gaulle's Appeal of 18 June
events.description: From exile in London, General Charles de Gaulle spoke on BBC radio to the French people as France was falling to Germany. He urged them to continue the fight and refuse to accept defeat.
events.significance: The broadcast is seen as the founding moment of the Free French movement. It made de Gaulle the voice of French resistance.

events.title: Sally Ride Becomes the First American Woman in Space
events.description: Astronaut Sally Ride launched aboard the Space Shuttle Challenger on mission STS-7. She served as a mission specialist on the six-day flight.
events.significance: Ride's flight broke a major barrier in the U.S. space program. It inspired generations of girls and women to pursue science and exploration.
